disk.eraseText: LordOS uses the whole disk: every partition and all its data are erased. This cannot be undone.
disk.freeBoot: LordOS becomes the first entry in the computer’s boot order. The other systems keep their entries.
disk.freeKeep: These stay untouched: every existing partition and its data ({parts}). The EFI partition {esp} is not formatted either: a new LordOS folder is added to it, and the boot files of other systems stay as they are.
disk.freeNo: Installing beside what is on this disk is not possible: {why}
disk.freeText: One new partition of {size} is created in free space. Keep a copy of anything important anyway: a disk can always fail.
disk.freeTitle: LordOS goes in the free space of {disk}
disk.freeUnderstand: I understand LordOS adds one partition and leaves the rest as it is
disk.none: No disk to install on was found.
disk.small: Too small: LordOS needs at least 8 GB.
disk.swapHint: A file on the disk used as extra memory.
disk.typeName: To confirm, type the disk name: {name}
disk.understand: I understand the whole disk will be erased
done.title: LordOS is installed
done.usb: Restart and remove the USB drive (or the install disc) when the computer turns off.
error.title: The installation failed
install.title: Installing LordOS…
language.regionHint: Dates, numbers and the language of Linux programs.
needAdmin: Installing needs the live system administrator account.
summary.layoutFree: One new partition of {size} (ext4) in free space · boot in the existing EFI partition
summary.layoutValue: GPT: BIOS boot 1 MB · EFI 512 MB (FAT32) · system (ext4) on the rest
summary.layoutValueEfi: GPT: EFI 512 MB (FAT32) · system (ext4) on the rest
summary.login: At boot the login screen appears: sign in with this user and password. Automatic login can be turned on in Settings → Users. The password is also used for sudo and administration tasks.
title: Install LordOS
user.errFullChars: The name cannot contain : , or line breaks.
user.errHost: Lowercase letters, numbers and -, not starting or ending with -.
user.errReserved: That name is used by the system.
user.errUser: Use lowercase letters, numbers, - and _, starting with a letter.
user.hostHint: How this computer appears on the network.
user.userHint: Lowercase letters, numbers, - and _. It will be an administrator (sudo).
welcome.text: This assistant installs LordOS on this computer’s disk. You will choose the language, keyboard, disk and your user. Installing erases the chosen disk, unless it has room to install beside what is there and you choose that.
welcome.title: Welcome to LordOS
